# load libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)

```

# support vector machine(SVM)
- is a suppervised machine learning algorthm used for both classification and regression task.
- svm woks by finding optimal boundary (hyperplane)
   that best separates data points into different classes while maximising the margin btn them
-



# load data set
```{r}
data(mtcars)
head(data)
```

# check structure
```{r}
str(mtcars)
```


# summary statistics
```{r}
describe(mtcars)
```



# check missing values
```{r}
colSums((is.na(mtcars)))
```



# split data
```{r}
set.seed(123)
split_index<-createDataPartition(mtcars$mpg, p=0.8, list=FALSE)
train_data1<-mtcars[split_index, ]
test_data1<-mtcars[-split_index, ]
```


# data dimension
```{r}
dim(train_data1)
dim(test_data1)
```

# scale the predictor valiables
```{r}
# separate predictors and targets
x_train<- train_data1[, -1]
y_train<-train_data1$mpg

x_test<-test_data1[, -1]
y_test<-test_data1$mpg


# standardization

preProc<- preProcess(x_train,
                      method =c("center", "scale"))
                     
                     x_train_scaled<-predict(preProc, x_train)
                     x_test_scaled<-predict(preProc, x_test)

```

# train SVM model
```{r}
svm_model<-svm(x=x_train_scaled,
              y=y_train,
              type="eps-regression",
              kernel="radial")
# view model
print(svm_model)
```

# make predictions
```{r}
predictions<-predict(svm_model, newdata=x_test_scaled)
head(predictions)

```

# evaluate model performance
### rmse
```{r}
rmse<-sqrt(mean((predictions - y_test)^2))
rmse
```


## mae
```{r}
mae<- mean(abs(predictions -y_test))
mae
```

### r2
```{r}
R2=cor(predictions, y_test)^2
R2
```


## actual vs predicted values
```{r}
results<-data.frame(actual=y_test,
predicted= round(predictions, 2)
)
results
```


### scatterplot of predictions
```{r}
plot(y_test,predictions, main="Actual vs Predicted",
     xlab="actual MPG",
     ylab="predicted mpg")
abline(0, 1, col="red", lwd=2)
```

## hyperparamater tuning for better accuracy
```{r}
set.seed(123)
turned_model<-tune(
  svm,
  mpg~.,
  data=train_data1,
  kernel= "radial",
  ranges=list(
    cost=c(0.1, 1, 10, 100),
    gamma=c(.001, .01, .1, 1)
  )
)
summary(turned_model)
```


## best model
```{r}
best_svm<- turned_model$best.model
pred_best<- predict(best_svm, test_data1)
rmse_best<- sqrt(mean((pred_best -test_data1$mpg)^2))
mae_best<- mean(abs(pred_best- test_data1$mpg))
rmse_best
mae_best
```

# SVM CLASSIFICATION
```{r}
data(iris)
set.seed(123)
 train_data2<-createDataPartition(
   iris$Species, p=0.8, list = FALSE)
 
 train<-iris[train_data2, ]
 test<-iris[-train_data2, ]
 
 svm_classifier<-svm(
   Species~.,
   data=train,
   kernel="radial"
   
 )
 
 pred_class<- predict(
   svm_classifier, test
 )
 confusionMatrix(pred_class, test$Species)
```

- TP = true positive for that class.

- TN = true negative for that class.

- FP = false positive for that class.

- FN = false negative for that class.

- N = total number of samples.

- Sensitivity: TP / (TP + FN). Of all real members of this class, how many did the model catch?

- Specificity: TN / (TN + FP). Of all real non-members, how many did the model correctly reject?

- Pos Pred Value: TP / (TP + FP). When the model predicts this class, how often is it correct?

- Neg Pred Value: TN / (TN + FN). When the model predicts “not this class,” how often is it correct?

- Prevalence: (TP + FN) / N. How common is this class in the actual data?

- Detection Rate: TP / N. What fraction of all samples are correctly predicted as this class?

- Detection Prevalence: (TP + FP) / N. What fraction of all samples are predicted as this class, right or wrong?
- Balanced Accuracy: (Sensitivity + Specificity) / 2. Fair average of catching real cases and avoiding false alarms.

# explanation on results above
- setosa: all metrics are 1.0000, so it is perfectly classified.

- versicolor: Sensitivity = 1.0000, so all real versicolor were caught.

- versicolor: Specificity = 0.9000, so some non-versicolor were wrongly called versicolor.

- versicolor: Pos Pred Value = 0.8333, so only 83.33% of versicolor predictions were correct.

- virginica: Sensitivity = 0.8000, so 20% of real virginica were missed.

- virginica: Specificity = 1.0000, so no other class was wrongly called virginica.

- virginica: Neg Pred Value = 0.9091, so some real virginica were predicted as “not virginica.”

- Balanced Accuracy: setosa = 1.0000, versicolor = 0.9500, virginica = 0.9000.
